generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology this runs through every literature review and essay. You reach past the discovery service into databases like PsycINFO and follow citation trails between key studies, then refine the search with Boolean operators and limiters so it stays precise. You weigh each study against its currency, authority and relevance to your question, and you repeat the cycle as your argument takes shape. Each search sharpens how you run the next.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students search for evidence on the same effect. One runs a quick discovery-service search and cites the first few results without checking their standing. The other searches PsycINFO, follows a key study's citations backwards and forwards, tightens the terms with Boolean logic and a peer-review limiter, then weighs each study against currency and authority. The second student's review is both wider and more rigorous, because she treats reaching, refining and judging as one practice.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, searching well is a continuing practice. You reach into databases and citation trails, refine for precision and recall, and judge each study against explicit criteria, on every review you write. Done this way, your evidence base is both fair to the field and ready to defend.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three strands are running as one practice: reaching widely, controlling the search, and judging what it returns.
_items.feedback: Yes. Extend, refine and evaluate worked together as one connected practice.

_items.text: That only one of the three moves was needed, and the others were wasted.
_items.feedback: Each move did real work: reaching, refining and judging all mattered.

_items.text: That evaluating what you find can replace searching widely in the first place.
_items.feedback: Reaching widely is a strand in its own right, not something evaluation removes.

_items.text: That the search is now finished and need never be repeated.
_items.feedback: Searching well is a cycle you repeat, not a single pass.
